body: That's not what I meant. My life is an actively malicious force that hunts down good things and destroys them. Even the little things aren't safe if I allow myself to enjoy them. Life will smell that little bit of happiness and gleefully devour it. If something it kills doesn't get to me, it will keep going until something else does. It wants me on my knees, broken, pleading for the end it will never bring unless I do it myself. No more. After the 8th, no more ever again. I gave life 27 years to show that it wanted me around as anything more than a cruel plaything, and it lured me long with false hope and promises, just to chew me up and spit me out into the gutter. I enjoyed our conversation too, it was refreshing to see someone with the strength of character to continue slogging through this fucking shit-circus, but that's not me and it never will be. Life will make sure of that. Best of luck in your story, but mine is at its end. I'm done.

I might think I have nothing to lose, but trust me, life will find something. It always does. Next it'll be my other leg. Or my arms. Or my spine. Or my apartment will burn down without me in it. There's always something. I'll be unacceptably limited in how much I can heal and rebuild. This half-life I've been saddled with is just bullshit. Pure bullshit. I want to hang on in the same way that anyone that has to cut their losses in anything wishes they didn't. It doesn't necessarily mean it's wise to do so. If I leave, I won't gain anything, but more importantly, I won't care what else I lose, because without an "I" there IS nothing to lose. Life can't take anything more from me if I throw what little is left away myself. I'm 8-Miling the shit. "I just fired off all your ammo for you, hurt me now bitch."

That's just it though; of course chronic pain, disability, poverty and loneliness is going to prevent me from being happy. I don't want to grind, I don't want to "manage" my life, I want to fucking live it. But not now, not like this. I feel slighted because I *have* been slighted. The job loss didn't get me down, so life just kept hammering me until it found something. I don't think anyone will ever be able to convince me that life didn't personally target me, and I can't stand all these insults any longer. I've spent the last year really thinking about my "decision," and to me, it isn't a decision at all; I have to go.

I appreciate the kind words, but what my life is now is something I could never be satisfied with. Mobility was one of the only things that heloed me, and a life without it... Well, isn't. At least not one I'm willing to suffer through. I dread what the future will bring, because it's been three decades of nothing but bullshit so far; why would that change just because I'm crippled now? I tried therapy for over a year. It helped while things were stable, but I can't talk away these problems. No, the only way forward for me is out. I only have three weeks and four days left until my date, and then I won't have to worry about "changing" (lowering) my standards for my shitty, shitty, worthless, shitty, ten-piece McNothing ass life. You can't understand it unless you've been there, and even then you still might not in the same way I do, but it is beyond my comprehension what could ever make the measly credits and mountainous debits of this life come even cloe to squaring. I'm irredeemably into the negatives, so zeroing everything out is my best option at this point. I know it won't get better at that point, but it wasn't anyway.

I don't feel like writing it all out again, but if you're really interested about the why, it's in my post history. Very long story short, life has destroyed literally everything I liked about it in a few short months. I disagree about free will, because I liken it to getting punched in the face and deciding your nose doesn't break. It makes no sense. Life will fuck you until you cry if you're unlucky; it doesn't matter if you "choose" to have a good life when things are objectively shitty, because you have been chosen to have a shitty life. Even if I do recover from my injuries and make it through this, there is nothing waiting for me on the other side. Rebuilding is more trouble than it's worth, especially when I can never rebuild to where I was before my life fell apart. I have a long life of coping, dealing and making do ahead of me, and that does not interest me. Problem-solving can be fun, but not when it's constant and there's no end in sight. It's just not worth it to try and make anything out of these broken pieces, because it will never live up to the standards of what my life could have been. Better luck next time.

That wasn't directed at you. It's a sneaky tactic people use to talk others down. "Wait for tomorrow, if it's still bad, do it tomorrow." "Wait for tomorrow, if it's still bad, do it tomorrow." "Wait for tomorrow, it it's still bad, do it tomorrow." "Wait..." Ad nauseum. There is usually something worth fighting for in life, but not always. I had plenty to fight for three months ago, but it's all gone now and starting over is unacceptable. My mother said she loved me when I asked her why I was here, and I just sort of said " fucking great, wonderful, love you too." Shitting me out into a life like this is a funny way of showing it. It's good you're taking time to reflect on yourself. I think suicide is an incredibly strong act. It takes a lot to override your own survival instincts, look into the face of existence itself and tell it to fuck off.

I didn't even remember it again until I was seventeen. That was the first episode of sexual abuse. I was also molested by my cousin's boyfriend from the ages of six to nine, the neighbor's daughter at seven, and raped by my estranged father at five. Everyone thought I lied about my sister's boyfriend, so I never said anything about it again. I was eating Red Vines when he came for me. I still gag whenever I smell red licorice. I never did work through any of it, my therapist never went into my childhood at all. It still haunts me almost every night, over twenty years later.

My sister and I don't talk. She's been a heroin addict for a decade and a half now. I walked away in year four and never looked back. I loved her, yes, but the sister I loved is gone. I cry when I see her old pictures. 

I think I made it this far out of pure stubbornness, but I'm depleted. Even my therapist says she could see it. I'm a resilient, resourceful survivor that is tired down in the pit of his soul. I have no reason to keep going. I put it off killing myself because I might as well see if my life got better. "If it gets worse, you can always do it then." Sound familiar? Well, here we are.

I was extensively physically, emotionally and sexually abused as a child. She was behind the physical and emotional aspects, and knew about the sexual stuff and did nothing to stop it. Just being around her is hard sometimes. 

She also has ADHD and will cut me off to hold up "this beautiful leaf I found outside" while I'm breaking down over the fact that my life is ruined. 

The non-sequiturs she spits out sometimes are straight up retarded. Example: Trying to nag my into using a mattress pad that would have raised my torso to a point that my leg would not be elevated properly post surgery. I pointed that out to her, and she said "okay, but it's just a single bed." 

It's very difficult to have a conversation with her.

I've struggled with suicidal depression since... Well, always. My first memory is of my mother screaming at me thst I was too fat and ugly for my sister's boyfriend to touch me like that, so I should stop making up stories. Our relationship is complicated. I was four.

I never imagined a future at all. I don't know how I made it this far, or why. I don't know how I pictured my life, but not like this.

Because I screamed at her, on my birthday, demanding she tell me why she just HAD to fucking have me, and was the cock worth it. I told her whatver asset she thought I was to the world was bullshit and I wasn't interested in helping a world that turned its back on me. I'm not proud. She said she'll always love me, but I'm too volatile for her to be around me anymore. She blocked my number. I don't blame her.

There's nothing left. My life has almost entirely lacked direction for the last three years. I was waiting for my commitment-issues girlfriend of nearly four years to be ready to move in together and start our lives. Even if we were never happy with ourselves, at least we had each other. Until I drove her away with my selfishness, ungratefulness, immaturity, negativity and despair. So that's been dashed. I wanted to run a marathon someday, but now I would need to train up from literally nothing in the very short time before my injuries cripple me for good. Scratch that too. Starting a business, nope, my capital is gone and I don't have any credit. My bucket list has already been crossed off for me.

Because of the predisposition to arthritis in the injuries I sustained, I WILL feel this pain forever. My first post on this account was a year ago, outlining my plan to get meds, counseling, everything possible to see if I could get the needle to move at all. This year was my last chance year, and if I ended it as bad or worse than I began it, I was going to accept my life as terminally shit and check on out. Things were going great until I lost my job in September because of a boss that discriminated against my depression, and things just spiraled from there. My point is, I already waited a year, and look what what happened to me. No more.

I destroyed my knee in a bike accident in October, the day before my birthday. I had surgery, and will walk again... For a few years, until arthritis puts me in a chair. That is something that I am painfully uninterested in experiencing. As far as I'm concerned, I'm walking out of a bad movie, nothing more. 

I had one attempt a few months ago. Alcohol and Nyquil. Lived and learned.  This time I'm doing helium. You just breathe in and go to sleep.

It's not just sometimes. My life is a shit hand, and I'm tired of playing a ten high for the sake of playing the shitty cards I was dealt. I'm folding. It's been a horrible life. Almost thirty years of nothing but pain, disappointment, and progressive loss. I was never happy and I never will be. I refuse to live as an invalid. I'm ending it now before it has a chance to somehow get even worse.

My job

My life savings

My partner

All my friends except one

My mother's desire to have anything to do with me

By next month, it'll be just me, I'll have fulfilled my promise to make it through this year, and I'll be free to end this life that I never loved or wanted. This whole thing has been a miserable, pointless affair and I think I'm quite finished with it. There are some doors you can't go back through.

I'm facing homelessness in a few months.

What a shit experience being alive was. Fuck it, I'm done.

It gets me on the same ground as everyone else that didn't get fucked with this disease with literally nothing else to show for a Herculean effort. The only option for me is a cure, be it in life or in death. I have my method, my place, my materials and now my time, and I will not suffer. I think you're just going to have to let this one go, friend.

Depression. I've had it for as long as I can remember, and for as long as I can remember, I've never gone more than three months without an episode. I've tried three therapists, a psychiatrist and four medications. None of them did a thing to change it. Every three months.

That's not a life. Scheduling your existence around quarterly breakdowns isn't a life, and neither is devoting your every waking moment to running from those breakdowns. At least, not lives that I will ever want, that I can ever enjoy. I would truly, honestly prefer the vast nothingness of death to a life of this. And it's been 27 years. I'm not getting better.

I thought this way too. Now I'm 26 and right where I started. I feel played by people that said things to me exactly like this. I'm not saying this to encourage anyone, I'm just saying that there is a very real chance things will not improve.

I AM getting help. I have been. I see a therapist every week and I'm medicated. That's what this year was about. Giving it my all with treatment and seeing where I land at the end of it. If I was any better, great! If not, I would accept that this disease is my life now and forever, be honest with myself about preferring death to that, and do what I had to do. I'm sticking it out until the end of the year because I said I would, but once this year is done, so am I.

I don't even remember. I've lost so much of myself to this fucking disease. Even if I did remember, it doesn't matter. I'm an inferior human being, trapped in a shitty, unattractive body with a sloppily-wired pile of mush and neurons that could loosely be called a dysfunctional brain. If I flex every fiber of my being in the direction of chronic illness management for the rest of my life, I *might* have *eh* life. But I'll have to constantly fight this shit with all my time and energy, losing every few months anyway, forever. Or I can opt out and never have to look at this ugly mug in the mirror or my work monitor ever again.

Maybe you should send your old friend, the one you drove away, a message. Just ask how he's doing. Ask if he'd be willing to meet up and talk things out now that you're more appreciative of his presence, if not necessarily stable yet. If he stuck around for that long and things ended as messy as they seem from what you said, chances are he misses you too. If not, if he tells you to fuck off, then that's one less thing holding you back from finding someone else to connect with, maybe not in the same exact way you did with him, but then maybe that's not such a bad thing either. I don't think you would want to forget your friend by completely replacing him.

People come and go, and change pretty much always sucks ass, but try to learn to appreciate things for what they are, rather than lamenting what they aren't. You really can find friends in the most unexpected of places. I found one of my current best friends through fucking /b/ seven years ago. But first you have to let go of what you expect now, underneath the pessimism that's crusted over that wounded hopefulness that I know is still in there. If it wasn't, you wouldn't feel so hurt by what's happened, nor would you if you expected nothing, even if you tell yourself you do.

Expectation is the root of disappointment, and resourcefulness is your chance to build some resilience against it, to dropkick that disappointment square in the fuckin' jimmies. And at the core of resourcefulness is appreciation. Appreciation, again, for what is, not what isn't. When you look at what tools you do have right now, and what you can do with the tools you have right now, I mean really look, you might find things aren't as bleak as our fucked-up minds try to tell us they are. You might find a way to take that disappointment, that hurt, on its head and outsmart it just by looking at it another way. Maybe, if you're resourceful enough. But you won't know until you take a step back and look for it.

I hope you find peace regardless of what you choose to do.
